source.title: Are All Linear Regions Created Equal?
source.authors: Matteo Gamba; Adrian Chmielewski-Anders; J. Sullivan; Hossein Azizpour; Mårten Björkman

record.tranche_reason: The authors explicitly reproduce the model-wise double-descent experimental setting and measure train and test error over a ResNet18 width sweep.
record.gate_note: The model-wise width-sweep results and the corresponding absolute-deviation and density measurements are included. Results cited from other studies are not recorded. Epoch-wise and sample-size double descent are not tested; the authors state they cap training at 400 epochs to avoid epoch-wise double descent.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the model-wise double-descent setting of Nakkiran et al. (ResNet18 width sweep, CIFAR-10, 20% label noise, Adam, no regularization). It reports train and test error that fall, rise to a peak at the interpolation threshold, then fall again.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that in model-wise double descent, overparameterization past the interpolation threshold reduces effective nonlinearity (locally similar linear regions) along with test error. They also conclude that linear-region density keeps rising and is a fragile complexity measure.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it reproduces Nakkiran et al. (2019)'s model-wise experimental setting: ResNet18 width sweep, CIFAR-10 with 20% corrupted labels, Adam, and no explicit regularization or augmentation. It caps training at 400 epochs to focus on model-wise descent and avoid epoch-wise double descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Absolute deviation (effective nonlinearity along data-driven paths) peaks at the interpolation threshold and declines during the second descent. Linear-region density instead rises monotonically with width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Past the interpolation threshold, larger networks learn functions with lower effective nonlinearity, even though raw linear-region counts keep increasing.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2022)
record.problems: The model-wise result is limited to one architecture family and one fixed label-corruption level. The width-sweep curves are presented in a figure and described qualitatively in the text; numerical curve values and uncertainty for these results are not stated.

untested.parts: Training is capped at 400 epochs explicitly to avoid epoch-wise double descent.
Only ResNet18 deep networks are swept; no other model classes.
No effective-model-complexity measure is used to predict peak location, and only the size axis is studied.
The width sweep uses only 20% label noise. Noise-level sweeps exist only for fixed-width networks and report nonlinearity, not double descent. Regularization is not tuned.
Other architectures and other noise levels are not tested; one setting only.
The curve is not re-expressed against an effective parameter count.

record.verdict_notes: The V5 label is dropped: absolute deviation correlating with test error does not test the claim that a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across axes. The double-descent error curves are given in a figure only. The figure caption says the top-panel measures are averaged over 3 seeds; seed count for the error curves is not stated. The paper is an original-adjacent replication, not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests the curve only for the reported ResNet18 width sweep on CIFAR-10 with 20% corrupted labels; it does not establish the pattern for other model families or settings.
The study limits training to 400 epochs to avoid epoch-wise double descent.
Training-set size is not varied near the interpolation threshold.
The double-descent sweep is limited to ResNet18 models, not multiple model classes.
The study examines absolute deviation along the model-size axis only; it does not test epochs or sample size, or whether one measure predicts peak location across axes.
The width sweep uses a fixed 20% label-corruption setting; it does not vary noise or regularization to test peak dependence, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.

The study compares region density with absolute deviation but does not re-express the curve using an effective number of parameters to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: ResNet18s
rows.size_stated: base width w ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 64}; standard ResNet18 at w = 64
rows.operation_detail: Sweep model base width and measure test error (0/1 loss).

conditions.value: no explicit regularization or data augmentation

rows.value: Decreases for w ≤ 4, rises for 4 < w ≤ 16, is highest at w = 16, then decreases for w > 16; numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: The text describes the fall-rise-fall pattern and identifies w = 16 as the interpolation threshold and test-error peak.

rows.subject: ResNet18s
rows.size_stated: base width w ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 64}; standard ResNet18 at w = 64
rows.operation_detail: Sweep model base width and measure training error (0/1 loss).
rows.value: Decreases for w ≤ 4; zero training error is achieved at w = 16 and remains zero for larger widths; numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: Training error identifies w = 16 as the interpolation threshold.
rows.check: This row locates the interpolation threshold (zero train error at w=16) for V1. It is not an independent fall-rise-fall result.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V1 from this measure alone. Training error reaches zero at w=16 and remains zero at larger widths; retain this row as interpolation-threshold evidence accompanying R1.
source_check.problem: Training error identifies interpolation but cannot independently establish V1's fall-rise-fall test-error pattern.

rows.subject: ResNet18s
rows.size_stated: base width w ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 64}; standard ResNet18 at w = 64
rows.operation_detail: Measure absolute deviation along data-driven paths across the model-width sweep.
rows.value: Low for underfitting networks (w ≤ 4), increases to a peak at the interpolation threshold (w = 16), then decreases; numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors report that absolute deviation follows the test-error second descent in this model-size sweep.
rows.check: Absolute deviation is a nonlinearity measure that tracks test error. It is not a measure used to predict where the peak falls along size, epochs or samples, and only one axis is studied. It does not test V5; moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: ResNet18s
rows.size_stated: base width w ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 64}; standard ResNet18 at w = 64
rows.operation_detail: Measure linear-region density along data-driven paths across the model-width sweep.
rows.value: Increases monotonically with model size; numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: This is a region-count result, not a test of V7's effective-parameter reparameterization.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 base width 1–64, CIFAR-10, 20% noisy labels, Adam, 400 epochs, no regularization or augmentation
relationships.reason: Test error falls (w≤4), rises to its maximum at w=16, where train error first reaches zero, then falls again (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: Test error decreased through w≤4, increased to its maximum at w=16 when training error first reached zero, then decreased again.
